Keeping peptides cool in Buckeye

Buckeye's own weather station kept records from March 1893 to November 2003, more than a century.6 The Western Regional Climate Center's summary of that record lines up with NOAA's current normals for Litchfield Park and Phoenix Sky Harbor like this:

Station and period July high July low January low Yearly precipitation
Buckeye, 1893 to 2003 record 107.1 °F6 74.4 °F6 34.6 °F6 7.70 inches7
Litchfield Park, 1991 to 2020 normals 106.5 °F8 81.2 °F8 42.9 °F8 8.18 inches9
Phoenix Sky Harbor, 1991 to 2020 normals 106.5 °F10 84.5 °F10 46.0 °F10 7.22 inches11

The old Buckeye record and the newer normals come from different stations and periods, so they are not a like-for-like comparison. Both put July afternoons above 106 °F. Litchfield Park, east of Buckeye at about 1,040 feet, averages 112.0 days a year at or above 100 °F, against 111.3 at Sky Harbor, and 7.1 nights at or below freezing, against 0.6.911 A parcel should come indoors soon after it arrives.

Heat is the obvious risk. A quieter one comes later, when a cold vial leaves the refrigerator or freezer. Bachem describes peptides as hygroscopic: they pull water from the air, and moisture taken up this way lowers the peptide content of the powder and may lower its stability.1213 Its advice is to let a cold container warm to room temperature in a desiccator before opening it.1213 GenScript singles out peptides containing aspartic acid, glutamic acid, lysine, arginine or histidine as prone to absorbing moisture, and advises keeping them in a desiccator in a tightly capped vial.14 Both makers say to take out what is needed quickly and reseal the container tightly.121314

Water is also part of why a vial's powder is not all peptide. Bachem says research peptides are typically more than 95 percent pure by HPLC, yet the powder may be only 70 to 90 percent peptide, with counter-ions and residual water making up the rest. That content has to be allowed for when making a solution of a set concentration.13 The reconstitution calculator handles the arithmetic, and the storage guide covers storage before and after mixing.

About Buckeye

Buckeye takes its name from the Buckeye Canal, laid out in May 1885 by Malie M. Jackson and partners and named for Jackson's native state of Ohio.15 The city dates its founding to March 1888, when its first post office was established, and it incorporated in 1929 with 440 acres, about 0.7 square miles.15 It now covers 396.12 square miles of land.2 Buckeye Days, a tradition the city says is still going strong, began in 1935 as Helzapoppin Days, started by the Buckeye Chamber of Commerce.15

Growth has been fast. The population estimate rose from 91,498 at the April 2020 base to 125,445 on July 1, 2025, about 37 percent, and 6,552 of those new residents, about 5.5 percent growth, came in the final year alone.1

Buckeye Hills Regional Park takes in 4,453 acres of open desert in the southwest Valley, with the Gila River's riparian corridor in view nearby, and the county lists the Joe Foss Shooting Complex with the park.16 Verrado, a master-planned community near Interstate 10 at Verrado Way, is home to a Banner Health Center offering primary care with on-site labs and X-rays.517

Health care in the city is expanding. Abrazo Health opened its three-story, 60,000-square-foot Buckeye Medical Office Building near Verrado in 2025.17 Abrazo calls it the first step toward a 27-acre medical campus that is to include an acute care hospital, and it has run an emergency center on Watson Road since 2011.17

The 2024 American Community Survey puts Buckeye's median age at 38.7, close to the county's 38.0, but children make up a larger share: 25.5 percent of residents are under 18, against 21.7 percent countywide.181920 Commutes are long, averaging 35.6 minutes against 27.1 for the county, and 6.7 percent of residents lack health insurance, below the county's 10.5 percent.212220

Frequently asked questions

Do you ship research peptides to Buckeye and Verrado?

Yes. Orders to Buckeye ship from the USA and Canada under the shipping policy used for every order across the United States, and that includes the Verrado community near Interstate 10.5 Census maps about 52 percent of the city's land to ZIP Code Tabulation Area 85326 and about 18 percent to 85396, with small parts in 85361, 85340, 85354 and 85343.3 If a parcel arrives damaged or incomplete, the returns page explains what to do.

How far is Buckeye from Phoenix?

About 33 miles in a straight line between the two cities' Census center points, with Buckeye to the west-southwest.2 Interstate 10 runs through Buckeye, and Banner Health places the city in the Southwest Valley of metro Phoenix.45 Orders ship to both cities the same way, and Peptides in Phoenix is the hub page that links every Maricopa County place we cover.

Can a lab in Buckeye order larger quantities?

Yes, through a wholesale account. Wholesale and bulk peptides explains how accounts work, and the wholesale application starts the process.
